remarks:
1. TO ALL WHOM IT MAY CONCERN: Notice is given that the 110-ft x 600-ft River Lock Chamber at New Cumberland L/D, Ohio River Mils 54.3, is unavailable for service. An inspection revealed that the upper lock gates are structurally inadequate for daily operations.

2. The 110-ft x 600-ft River Lock Chamber will be closed to all navigation traffic until repairs can be made to the gates.

3. A revised Notice to Navigation Intersts will be issued once the repairs to the lock gates are made and the river lock chamber is back in operation. 

4. Navigators are requested to use caution when entering or leaving the land lock chamber during the closure of the river lock chamber to prevent a complete shutdown of navigation.

 

FOR THE DISTRICT ENGINEER:
title: CLosure of the River Lock Chamber at New Cumberland L/D, Ohio River, Mile 54.3

remarks:
1.       TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN: Notice is given that a Construction Contractor working for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Pittsburgh District, will be performing work on the Middle Wall at Montgomery Locks and Dam. This work will necessitate closure of the main 110-ft x 600-ft lock chamber.

2.       Starting on June 24, 2019, the 110-ft x 600-ft Primary Lock Chamber at Montgomery Locks and Dam will be closed from 0700 to 1900, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal Holidays, until further notice.

3.       Upon daily re-openings, tows in queue will be locked in order of arrival. For the period up until July 12, 2019, the Pittsburgh District will try and utilize any breaks in construction throughout the day, to perform a lock operation to reduce the number of tows in queue.

4.       Construction work at Montgomery will extend into 2020. Changes to the closure structure will be communicated via a revised navigation notice and/or marine radio.

 

FOR THE DISTRICT ENGINEER:
title:

remarks:

2) DELAYS TO NAVIGATION AUXILIARY CHAMBER CLOSED: 

05 October 2026 - 0900 to 1500 EST (6 hours)

06 October 2026 - 0800 to 1600 EST (8 hours)

07 October 2026 - 0900 to 1500 EST (6 hours)

08 October 2026 - 0800 to 1600 EST (8 hours)

09 October 2026 - 0900 to 1500 EST (6 hours)

 

3) The closures are required to support ongoing contractor work. 

 

4) PROCEDURE: The  110-ft x 1200-ft primary chamber will remain in operation during the auxiliary chamber closures. 

 

5) Mariners in the area are required to monitor channel 13 for updates or information during the closure periods.
title: Pike Island Locks and Dam Ohio River, Mile 84.2, Intermittent Closures of the Auxiliary Chamber

remarks:
1.TO ALL WHOM IT MAY CONCERN: Notice is given that the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers will be closing the 110-ft x 600-ft primary chamber at Montgomery Lock and Dam to support ongoing contractor work. 

 

2. DELAYS TO NAVIGATION:  The chamber will be closed beginning at 7:00 AM and continue for a 24-hour period (ending at 7:00 AM the following day) on the following dates:

 

  • April: 27 and 29
  • May: 4, 7, 11, 14, 18, 21,  27, 30
  • June: 2, 8, 11, 15, 18

 

These closures will cause a river shutdown as the auxiliary chamber is no longer functional.

 

3. Mariners are requested to monitor VCF Channel 13 for updates during the closure periods.
title: Montgomery Lock and Dam (L/D), Ohio River, Mile 31.7, Closure of 110-ft X 600-ft Primary Chamber

remarks:
1. All navigation interests are advised of an obstruction (embedded metal) at the Main Lock lower intermediate wall bulkhead slot, just below the intermediate wall miter gate. The embedded metal corner protection on the upstream side of the bulkhead slot protrudes into the lock chamber roughly 3 inches from the wall. It is considered a hazard to passing tows and all mariners are advised from now until further notice to favor the east wall so as not to rub in this area of the main lock. The district will advice when repairs are made.

2. All navigation interests should be alert for, and abide by, any special instructions that may be issued by the Lockmaster during these timeframes.

 

FOR THE DISTRICT ENGINEER:
title:
OBSTRUCTION (EMBEDDED METAL)
Locks 27, Upper Mississippi River Mile 185.5

remarks:
1.  Recent project condition surveys at Muskegon Harbor, MI, indicate shoaling in the navigation channel. 

 

2.  Shoaling is present across the entrance of the channel throughout project stationing -26+00 to -27+00 with shoaling present on both north and south sections of the channel entrance flare.  Depths in the center of the channel range from 0 to 7.5 feet above project depth. 

 

3.  Shoaling present in the north half of the channel entrance flare is shallower, but the entire shoal may be a limiting factor for vessels accessing the harbor. 

 

4.  The most recent project condition survey is attached to this notice. 

 

5. Questions regarding this notice may be directed to the Grand Haven Operations Manager, Elizabeth Wilkinson at (616)240-7989.
title: REPORTED SHOALING - MUSKEGON HARBOR, MI
